newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end up on LME gains.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end up on LME gains.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended mostly up on Tuesday after overnight gains on the London Metal Exchange (LME), traders said.
The most actively traded October 1997 contract ended at 23,390 yuan ($2,820) per tonne, rising 90 yuan. It opened at 23,380 yuan, hitting an intraday high of 23,440 and a low of 23,350 yuan.
July rose 30 to 22,770, August 70 to 22,980, September 110 to 23,190, November 80 to 23,450 but December fell 100 to 23,450 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume fell to 30,880 from 53,370 tonnes.
Copper opened higher and moved at high levels for most of the session, backed up by the overnight LME gains, traders said.
Traders said the LME gains, small though they were at only $2 up to $2,588 a tonne for three-months, boosted the confidence of long position holders in Shanghai.
"The LME was the major factor on Tuesday but volume was thin, indicating investors were not certain about the short-term market trend," one trader said.
"But copper is unlikely to drop sharply in the short term with many investors believing LME copper will maintian its uptrend," he added.
Physical prices are around 23,000 yuan level in the Shanghai area, slightly up from Monday's 22,900 yuan.
Low domestic prices were cited by Chinese metals industry officials as a reason China will deliver up to 10,000 tonnes of copper into LME warehouses in Singapore over the next month.
Official of China National Nonferrous Metal Import and Export Corp (CNIEC) said China wants to take advantage of the current high world prices.
Western and Chinese trading sources said, however, that simultaneous annoucements by CNIEC officials in Singapore and Beijing indicated a coordinated effort to push down world prices.
Shanghai traders said the LME would be an important factor influencing local copper prices in the short term in the absence of domestic market-moving news.
"Late-maturing contracts are likely to move above the 23,000 yuan level in the next few days waiting for fresh news," a second trader said.
July fell 20 to 14,310, August shed 100 to 14,300, September did not trade and October dropped 350 to 14,600 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume fell to 1,260 tonnes from 1,640 tonnes.
